name: Glaucoma-Ectopia Lentis-Microspherophakia-Stiff Joints-Short Stature Syndrome
aliases: Glaucoma with Ectopia Lentis and Microspherophakia Syndrome

criteria.description: Displacement or malposition of the ocular lens (ectopia lentis)
Presence of abnormally small and spherical lenses (microspherophakia)
Elevated intraocular pressure leading to optic nerve damage (glaucoma)
Clinically significant joint stiffness and limited range of motion
Height significantly below the 3rd percentile for age and sex

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of ectopia lentis, microspherophakia, and glaucoma
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Additional features such as stiff joints and short stature support diagnosis but are not mandatory.

imaging: Slit-lamp examination showing microspherophakia and ectopia lentis
Optical coherence tomography (OCT) for optic nerve assessment
Radiographs showing joint stiffness and skeletal abnormalities
other: Visual field testing indicating glaucomatous damage

distinguishingFeatures: Tall stature rather than short stature
Systemic cardiovascular involvement with aortic root dilation
More prominent brachydactyly and joint stiffness

redFlags: Rapidly progressive glaucoma leading to vision loss
Sudden onset of lens dislocation causing acute visual impairment
references: Orphanet: Glaucoma-ectopia lentis-microspherophakia-stiff joints-short stature syndrome - ORPHA:2084
Faivre L, et al. ADAMTSL4 mutations in ectopia lentis and microspherophakia. Am J Hum Genet. 2009.
Weill-Marchesani syndrome and related disorders: clinical and molecular aspects. GeneReviews, 2020.
